clue.text: Where lies circulating around famous Downing Street figure, might this have extra traction?

indicators.note: one piece goes around another, so the rearranged letters enclose the Roman figure
letters circulating are moving round into a new order, so the words where lies are rearranged

parts.note: the Prime Minister lives at No 10 Downing Street, and ten is X in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A political riddle: a liar circling the Prime Minister's residence, and something with extra grip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Downing Street figure' looks like the PM, but it is the number on the door, 10, written as X; 'circulating' rearranges WHERE LIES into SIWHEELER and X goes 'around' inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A vehicle with six driven wheels has more contact with the ground than a four-wheeled one, so better grip.

clue.text: Mastermind tune for worms

parts.note: to mastermind a scheme is to plan it
an aria is a song or tune in an opera

explanation.surface: The quiz show Mastermind's theme music is apparently for worms.
explanation.walkthrough: Mastermind is a famous British TV quiz, but here it is the verb: to plan.
explanation.definitionFit: Planarians are flatworms, and this Latin plural names a group of those freshwater flatworms.

clue.text: Individual absorbed by course, virtually complete

indicators.note: something absorbed is taken inside, so the letter goes into the shortened course
virtually means almost all, so the final letter of the course word is dropped

parts.note: an entree is a course of a meal
I, as in one, an individual person

explanation.surface: A single person on a course of study who is nearly finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'virtually' trims ENTREE to ENTRE, and I is 'absorbed by' it.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something whole, with nothing missing.

clue.text: Guns raised for quarry in glen?

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means read upwards, so the letters go backwards

parts.note: gats is old slang for guns

explanation.surface: Hunters raise their rifles at their prey in a Scottish valley.
explanation.walkthrough: A glen is a Scottish valley; the question mark marks the deer as one example of what is hunted there.
explanation.definitionFit: A male red deer is the classic hunted animal of the Scottish Highlands.

clue.text: One sport he worked on, nearing defeat

indicators.note: letters worked on are reshaped, so one sport he is rearranged

explanation.surface: A sportsman keeps working at his one sport while close to losing.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom from boxing, where a fighter driven back against the ring's boundary is close to losing.

clue.text: Sloth near Ealing fed last of spaghetti

indicators.note: fed means given something to take in, so a letter goes inside

parts.note: Acton is a district right next to Ealing in west London, so near Ealing is in Acton

indicators.note: last of signals the final letter of the word spaghetti

explanation.surface: A lazy creature in west London eats its pasta.
explanation.walkthrough: Ealing and Acton are neighbouring west London districts; 'fed' puts I, the 'last of' spaghetti, into IN ACTON.
explanation.definitionFit: Sloth is laziness, a state of doing nothing at all.

clue.text: See 18
Report scale and method as liquid strained

indicators.note: report suggests speaking out, so what is said has the same sound as the entry

parts.note: to scale is to weigh, and a method is a way; both words sound the same

explanation.surface: A recipe instruction: report the scale and method when straining liquid.
explanation.walkthrough: Two words are said aloud here, and both sound identical: WEIGH (scale) and WAY (method).
explanation.definitionFit: The watery part of milk left behind when curds are separated and the liquid is drained off.

clue.text: Seat: I offered support for member not returned PM

parts.note: a sling is support offered for an injured arm, a limb or member

indicators.note: returned means turned back, so the word not is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written before being turned
Lord North was Prime Minister of Great Britain from 1770 to 1782

explanation.surface: A politician muses on being offered support yet never becoming Prime Minister.
explanation.walkthrough: The seat is Jeremy Corbyn's constituency: he led Labour but was 'not returned PM'. Lord North, an 18th-century Prime Minister, supplies the last part.
explanation.definitionFit: A Parliamentary constituency is called a seat in the House of Commons.

clue.text: See 9
See 20
London borough cut back foreign money

parts.note: to hack is to cut roughly

indicators.note: back means the word for the money is read in reverse

parts.note: the yen is the Japanese currency

explanation.surface: A London council slashing its overseas funding.
explanation.definitionFit: A borough in north-east London, one of the capital's thirty-two local authorities.

clue.text: Clifftop home creepy, we hear?

indicators.note: we hear means the clue is about what is said, the sound of a word

parts.note: creepy means eerie, unsettling

explanation.surface: Someone describes a house on a cliff as spooky.
explanation.definitionFit: An eagle or other bird of prey builds its nest high on a crag; that nest is its home.

clue.text: Endless suffering: Boris's heart consumed by power issue

parts.note: P is the standard abbreviation for power in physics

indicators.note: consumed by means swallowed into, so a letter goes inside

parts.note: an edition is an issue of a newspaper

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its central letter

explanation.surface: A political lament: Boris's heart eaten up by an issue of power, an endless torment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'consumed by' puts R, the 'heart' of Boris, inside EDITION.
explanation.definitionFit: Damnation in hell is eternal torment, a punishment without end.

clue.text: Boris, penning newspaper material that's shabby, is for the practical approach

indicators.note: penning means enclosing as in a pen, so the other pieces go inside

parts.note: Boris Johnson was the Prime Minister, PM, when this puzzle appeared
a rag is slang for a low-quality newspaper
a mat is a floor covering that gets worn and trodden on, a scruffy piece of material

explanation.surface: Boris, writing for a scruffy newspaper, favours being practical.
explanation.walkthrough: Boris stands for the PM, his job when this appeared; 'penning' looks like writing but means enclosing.
explanation.definitionFit: A philosophy of dealing with things sensibly and realistically rather than by theory.

clue.text: Stallion's back on course — whereas this one isn't

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter

parts.note: a starter is the first course of a meal

explanation.surface: A racing tip: a stallion back on the course, while another horse is absent.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads off the surface: 'this one' is not on course at all, being a horse that never races.
explanation.definitionFit: Something with no chance of success, originally a horse entered for a race that fails to run.

clue.text: Backtrack twice and workers lit up by party leader? I don't believe you!

indicators.note: twice means the piece is used two times in a row

parts.note: a track is a rail, and rail written back gives the needed letters

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: ants are the classic crossword workers, as worker ants
something lit up is burning, alight

explanation.surface: A party leader backtracking twice and workers set ablaze, and someone crying disbelief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backtrack' splits as back + track: RAIL turned round. 'by' places the leader's P beside ANTS.
explanation.definitionFit: A playground taunt thrown at someone thought to be telling fibs.

clue.text: Final drink full of street talk

indicators.note: full of means holding inside, so the street and talk pieces go into the drink

parts.note: to lap is to drink as a cat does
gas is idle chatter, talk

explanation.surface: A last pub drink accompanied by street slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Describes an effort made at the very end, at the last possible moment.

clue.text: In fun, absolute ruler's beginning to splash out — he can certainly afford it!

indicators.note: splash out suggests letters thrown about, so these words are rearranged
beginning signals the first letter of the word ruler's

explanation.surface: An absolute monarch spends lavishly for fun, being able to afford it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'splash out' looks like spending, but it is the signal to rearrange IN FUN, ABSOLUTE and R.
explanation.definitionFit: The monarch of the small oil-rich South-East Asian state is one of the world's richest people.

clue.text: Are various small birds travelling west, after starling initially again takes over

indicators.note: after places one piece following another in the answer
various suggests different arrangements, so the letters of are are mixed
initially signals the opening letter of starling
in an across clue, travelling west means reading right to left

parts.note: emus are large flightless Australian birds

explanation.surface: Assorted small birds fly west after a starling, and the flock takes over again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'travelling west' reverses S EMUS to SUMES, which comes 'after' the S of starling.
explanation.definitionFit: To take on a role or responsibility once more.

clue.text: Question put to liquidator by business, seriously?

definitions.text: Question put to liquidator by business
definitions.meaning: a liquidator winds up a failing firm, so the firm might ask whether it is about to be closed
an incredulous retort meaning ... joking with me

explanation.walkthrough: The first reading takes the phrase literally: a liquidator's job is winding up companies.
explanation.definitionFit: A colloquial way to ask if someone is teasing or kidding.

clue.text: Radioactive element in preservative for good health

indicators.note: in places the element's symbol inside the preservative

parts.note: salt has long been used to preserve food
U is the chemical symbol for uranium

explanation.surface: A warning about uranium in a food preservative, for the sake of health.
explanation.definitionFit: The French toast when raising a glass, wishing everyone well.

clue.text: Those speaking for author

definitions.meaning: Dorothy L ... wrote the Lord Peter Wimsey detective novels

explanation.definitionFit: Speakers of words, and the surname of a celebrated English crime writer.

clue.text: Middle 2 from 4 (x 2) for shipment

indicators.note: the middle two letters are taken away from the word for the number

parts.note: 4 is four in words
times two: the 4 doubled gives eight

explanation.surface: A cryptic sum of numbers and multiplication standing in for a shipment.
explanation.walkthrough: The 4 does double duty: FOUR loses its middle two letters, and 4 'x 2' is EIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods carried by ship, lorry or plane are cargo.

clue.text: See 16
Was PM unprejudiced, where only the elite accommodated?

parts.note: Theresa May was Prime Minister from 2016 to 2019
fair means impartial, without prejudice

explanation.surface: A question about whether a former PM was impartial in a place housing only the elite.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the exclusive West London district, one of the dearest addresses in the capital.
explanation.definitionFit: A wealthy area of central London famed for luxury hotels and grand houses.

clue.text: See 20
Discuss roads home

indicators.note: to discuss is to talk, so the word is spoken

parts.note: roads are routes

explanation.surface: Talking over the roads to get home.
explanation.walkthrough: Said in the British way, ROUTES and the answer sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Your origins, the place you come from, is where you belong.

clue.text: Back to basics here, as Conservative taking drugs?

parts.note: a square is a conventional, old-fashioned person
on as in on medication, taking it
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Would a Tory on drugs be back to basics?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back to basics' was John Major's 1990s Conservative slogan, so Conservative looks political; it means a square.
explanation.definitionFit: The starting point to which you return when everything must be begun again.
